title: CLICK3R: Interactive Stereo 3D Reconstruction with Sparse Correspondence Clicks
claim: A baseline reconstruction fails under hard conditions; adding a few sparse user correspondences to the same model recovers correct geometry.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right: input with clicks, baseline output, our output
description: Three panels read left to right. Panel (a) stacks two photos of a teal and pink BMX bike on a wooden deck, taken from different viewpoints. Colored dots and lines join matching points across the two views: a blue pair and a red pair. Panel (b), in a black frame, shows the baseline point-cloud reconstruction without clicks. The bike and deck are fragmented, misaligned and sparse, and the camera frustums sit in the wrong places. Panel (c), in a black frame, shows the reconstruction with clicks. The bike is coherent, the deck is a clean planar surface, and the camera pyramids are plausibly placed. Blue and red markers appear in both 3D panels, so the reader can see where the clicks land. Captions below each panel bold the words 'without' and 'with' to stress the contrast. The eye goes first to the colored click lines, then to the messy panel (b) and the clean panel (c).
caption: Overview. Given (a) an image pair and sparse correspondences (colored dot clicks), \mmethod{} conditions DUSt3R [ref] to produce accurate 3D reconstruction. (b) DUSt3R fails on a scene with limited overlaps. (c) With as few as two clicks, \mmethod{} recovers correct geometry.
abstract: Despite impressive progress, existing feed-forward large 3D reconstruction models produce a single, irrevocable prediction. When these models fail, there is no mechanism to correct their mistakes. To address this limitation, we introduce Click3R, a framework for interactive geometric correction of feed-forward models using sparse human correspondence clicks. Given an image pair and a small set of cross-view point correspondences provided by a user, Click3R injects geometric constraints into the 3D reconstruction networks through a lightweight point correspondence adapter, enabling the model to resolve ambiguities in challenging scenarios such as repetitive textures, symmetric structures, large viewpoint changes, or textureless regions. To evaluate interactive reconstruction, we curate a challenging benchmark specifically designed to expose failure modes of existing feed-forward 3D reconstruction methods. Experiments show that Click3R reduces reconstruction error with as few as a single correspondence click, improving performance on both standard and our curated benchmarks. Our results highlight that sparse human interaction provides an effective and practical mechanism for correcting geometric reconstruction errors.
